summary: Close P3 by executing tracked fulfillment reservations transactionally during warehouse failover, qualifying that execution in the deployed release topology, and resolving repository release-license metadata without weakening independent release gates.

impacts.evidence: Fulfillment allocations use organization/workspace composite keys and FORCE RLS; failover execution occurs after tenant-scoped incident claim.
Allocation evidence contains order/offer/warehouse identifiers but no credentials or free-form customer PII; retained release evidence remains synthetic.
Additive fulfillment-allocation GET/POST/read operations are declared in OpenAPI and regenerated SDKs.
Adds commerce.fulfillment.allocation_changed.v1 at version 1 and a dedicated fulfillment transport topic; existing events are unchanged.
Connector SDK types/capabilities are unchanged by P3.
Expand migration 000074 adds allocation ownership plus additive incident execution counters; it does not rewrite legacy inventory/order rows.

Reservation mutations are locked, exact and tenant-scoped; release workflow now blocks build on deployed runtime qualification; repository LICENSE metadata is explicit while independent scanner/provenance gates remain fail-closed.
Failover executes only tracked immutable order-item reservations on explicit routes with sufficient locked destination ATP; ambiguity becomes needs_attention.
Replacement allocations retain incident_id/replaces_allocation_id and both inventory/allocation outbox events preserve source-to-destination execution lineage.
One-active-allocation-per-order-item plus deterministic failover idempotency prevents duplicate active ownership after retries/restarts.
Webhook delivery contracts do not change; new fulfillment events use the existing Outbox/Kafka/Inbox projection path.
Runtime qualification records reservation release/destination reserve/allocation lineage in addition to prior broker/database recovery and load evidence.
Migration 000074 is expand-only; rollback is application-first and retains allocation/incident evidence. Release CI requires restart, restore and upgrade qualification.
Migration, event fixture, SDK, inventory repository, release workflow and deployed-image qualifier checks cover P3; external hosted Ruleset/OIDC facts remain separately evidenced.
